subject.title: cron: webhook bearer token is attached to any job-supplied delivery.to host

question: Should cron webhook bearer delivery fail closed for job-record destinations until operators allowlist trusted hosts, or should OpenClaw preserve unconditional delivery by default and leave protection opt-in?
rationale: Both choices materially affect existing operators: fail-closed protects the SecretRef boundary but requires an upgrade action, while compatibility-first retains a path for an agent-influenced job record to route the credential externally.

options.title: Fail closed with guided recovery
options.body: Withhold the bearer for job-record destinations unless an operator-owned allowlist permits the host, and provide Doctor and runtime guidance for the required configuration.

options.title: Preserve compatibility by default
options.body: Continue attaching the bearer when no allowlist is configured, while documenting and recommending an explicit opt-in host restriction.

options.title: Pause the rollout design
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a narrower trust model avoids both the disclosure and an upgrade-time authentication break.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with guided recovery
recommendation.body: Withhold the bearer for job-record destinations unless an operator-owned allowlist permits the host, and provide Doctor and runtime guidance for the required configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant current-main cron/Gateway owner must make the security-versus-upgrade contract decision; this review could not complete history attribution.
